summary: Phase 1 (Player-Business + Inventory) — player-employees fully integrated. Wrote /app/backend/tests/test_phase1_player_employment.py (11 tests, all PASS) covering: hourly wage model end-to-end (market.base_hourly_wage + roles[]; OfferBody/WageBody wage_per_hour through offer→re-offer→accept→raise; notification text contains $X/h and previous wage on re-offer), role from staffing + fit (bad role falls back to first staffing role, applicant_snapshot exposes role_fit/fit_label/role_matches_staffing, off-staffing offer flagged), coverage integration (metrics.staffing[].player_have, metrics.player_employee_count, metrics.unmatched_player_count), per-shift output + net impact (POST /jobs/employment/{id}/work → fast-forward activity → /game/state resolves; emp.last_shift={hours,wage,revenue,net,productivity}; business.history kind=shift with amount=rev-wage; cash+debt mirror net; owner notification 'worked a 4h shift' with +$rev − $wage = net); low-skill/exhausted player yields net<wage (negative-leaning); /jobs/current returns {npc, player_jobs} with wage_per_hour/role/total_hours_worked; withdraw blocks subsequent offer/accept (both 400) and notifies owner. Updated /app/backend/tests/test_phase_c_employment.py + test_phase_c_fixes.py + test_phase_c_hours_promotion.py to wage_per_hour + lowercase staffing roles + notifications?limit=200 to defeat rolling-window flake, and fixed test_phase_c_employment asserting old 'base_shift_wage' → 'base_hourly_wage'. Full regression: 48/48 PASS (test_phase_c_employment 18, test_phase_c_fixes 13, test_phase_c_hours_promotion 6, test_phase1 11). Frontend Playwright (real preview URL https://grind-nation.preview.emergentagent.com): BusinessManage PlayerHiring shows emp-net-{id} 'Last shift (4h): +$41 revenue − $90 wage = net $-49' (verified), raise-send-{id}/fire-emp-{id} render; Employees tab has emp-list-player-{id} subsection; Finances tab finance-history labels each row BOOKING (kind=shift) vs FORECAST (kind=accrual) with per-shift label 'Mara Vance — 4h cashier shift -$49'. JobMarket cards show 'From $14/h' and 'Hiring: Cashier'; apply-role dropdown populates from staffing. CurrentJob shows 'Player-Business Employment' card with '$22.5/H', role, '4h Worked', 'Paid $22.5/h at the end of each shift (e.g. $90 for 4h)', WORK SHIFTS / MANAGE link, and cur-emp-{id} present. withdraw-app-{id} button not visible during run because mara had no pending app at that moment (she was actively employed); backend coverage of withdraw via TestWithdrawApplication explicitly verifies the UI path's contract (200 → status=withdrawn → owner notif → 400 on offer/accept).
critical_code_review_comments: employment.complete_player_shift L191-192: revenue = wph * hours * output_multiplier * productivity; net = revenue - wage. This correctly makes the business OWNER bear the risk of a bad hire — high-skill employee yields positive net, low-skill/exhausted yields negative. Verified empirically (mara healthy+sales-skilled → +rev, kiri at health=25/fatigue=90/sales lvl 1 → productivity ≤1.0, net < wage).

employment.complete_player_shift L207-209: when biz cash goes negative, the overflow is absorbed by biz.debt and cash clamped to 0. Test adapted to assert (cash_delta - debt_delta) == net, which mirrors this correctly. Good design — keeps cash non-negative while still recording the obligation.

employee_engine.business_metrics L46-66: PLAYER_PRESENCE=0.6 part-time weighting feels right — a single player counts as 0.6 FTE toward coverage, not a full 1.0, since players don't continuously work. Folded into both metrics() (UI snapshot) and resolve_business() (P&L coverage formula) — consistent.

employee_engine.business_metrics L74-75: player_employee_count and unmatched_player_count both surfaced — frontend can render a 'X player employee(s), Y in off-staffing roles' summary; currently BusinessManage shows player_have inside staffing rows but no explicit unmatched count UI. Minor — not blocking.

server.py L1716-1721 offer_player: role defaults to a.get('role','staff') when body.role is None; matches=role in role_ids stored on the application as role_matches_staffing. Good — owner can override role at offer time and the staffing-match flag travels through to the UI.

server.py L1650-1660 withdraw_business_application: idempotent guard via status ∈ {pending, offered} → 400 'Nothing to withdraw' otherwise; owner-side notification 'Applicant withdrew'. Subsequent offer (1707-1713) and accept (1614-1619) both check status and 400 correctly — withdrawn apps are fully terminal.

server.py L1772 raise_player: prev = emp.get('wage_per_hour') or wage_per_shift/4.0 — robust fallback for legacy docs from before migrate_player_employment_hourly() ran. decorate_employment() L211-212 mirrors this fallback. Both layers good.

server.py L2108-2112 migrate_player_employment_hourly: one-shot startup migration that derives wage_per_hour from wage_per_shift/4. Re-running is safe (only matches docs without wage_per_hour). Verified: 0 docs missing wage_per_hour after migration ran.

server.py L1492 WageBody only accepts wage_per_hour — old per-shift clients would 422. Acceptable since the entire frontend was migrated to hourly. Worth keeping a brief deprecation note if the API is consumed externally.

Finance history (BusinessManage finance-history): all NEW entries carry kind ∈ {accrual, shift} with amount + (rev, exp, net) on accrual, and (rev, wage, amount=rev-wage) on shift. Pre-migration entries without kind are tolerated; recommend running a one-shot history backfill (tag old entries kind='accrual') to remove the None values from view — minor cleanup.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/test_phase_c_hours_promotion.py (wage_per_shift → wage_per_hour; roles lowercased; notifications calls use ?limit=200)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Phase 1 fully verified. For future phases (2-5: training, role editor, labels/tooltips, inventory, equipment, products) the new test fixtures dovan_h/mara_h/kiri_h + _wipe_applications(biz, *pids) helper in test_phase1_player_employment.py are reusable. To fast-forward a player shift: POST /jobs/employment/{id}/work → db.players.update_one({id: pid}, {$set: {'current_activity.ends_at': past_iso}}) → GET /api/game/state. The notifications endpoint paginates with ?limit (default 40, max effectively 200+) — use ?limit=200 when asserting count deltas over long runs. Pre-Phase-1 business.history entries may have kind=None (stale); current write paths tag every new entry, but a one-shot backfill would be nice (non-blocking). Pytest needs '-o addopts=' override because pytest.ini sets xdist 'loadscope' addopts that conflict on rerun.
